questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me that the people were speaking English, that I could get far away and that the university had interesting units.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, there were many introduction events.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a person we always could email, plenty of information at the introduction events, and actually had the option of getting to know an Australian through the “Mates abroad” program.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find accomodation, but the prices are even worse than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Go for student dorms. They are cheaper and you get more friends!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just looked up the units that I wanted and applied for them through an email to our contact person. If it was then accepted, it appeared on a website where I then could choose my schedule if the same unit had multiple available hours.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could write to our contact person about everything and she would answer within 1-2 days.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100%. I got everything I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time choosing units, as there are so many.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did two master units and two “honors” units, which is on a level that is technically above bachelor level, but not advanced enough for them to call master.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was greater variation between the units. One unit gave us a ton of videos and an online quiz before we then later in the week met up to do exercises regarding the same subject as the videos and the quiz. Another had no preparation but just worked through four papers and then taught us the theory relevant for the papers along the way. It varied a lot.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: PHYS4016, PHYS4126, CSYS5010, CSYS5040

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend PHYS4016 and CSYS5040. PHYS4016 gives a great perspective on how to treat data correctly and has a very intuitive way of teaching. CSYS5040 offers great freedom and primarily is about bombarding the student with methods that could then be used in the final project of this unit.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Dining out was a bit more expensive than expected, but public transport was much cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could join multiple sports clubs and clubs related to everything from board games to physics and country of origin.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You should definitely join the academic club related to your study, as they have many social events where you can meet likeminded people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Blue Mountains is supposed to be beautiful. The Royal Botanical Garden is amazing as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very much, as the culture is very similar to the “northern European culture” I am used to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join as many clubs as possible! You don't have to show up if you end up not liking it, and most of them are free.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing in the beginning how all the social and sports clubs went through the university.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open they were! People I barely knew invited me over for Christmas!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-	Join as many clubs as possible
-	Live in student dorms – this will also give you a lot of friends!
-	Remember to “be a tourist” as much as possible!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to get an Opal Concession card as soon as possible, as this will cut the public transport expenses in half.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The kindness I was met with and the amazing nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably to find the balance between school and fun – it is easy to prioritize school a little too much.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
